headline: India women's team refuses Asia Cup trophy from Naqvi after final win
summary: Following their eighth Women's Asia Cup title, the Indian side declined to accept the trophy from ACC president Mohsin Naqvi in Dubai.
details: India secured their eighth Women's Asia Cup title by defeating Sri Lanka by 72 runs in the final held in Dubai. However, the victory was overshadowed by a diplomatic standoff during the post-match presentation.

The Indian team refused to receive the trophy or their medals from Asian Cricket Council (ACC) president Mohsin Naqvi, who is also the chairman of the Pakistan Cricket Board and Pakistan's interior minister.

The ceremony was delayed by nearly 50 minutes. While Sri Lankan players received their runners-up medals and cheque from Naqvi, the Indian players abruptly ended their part of the ceremony without collecting the award.
This incident mirrors a similar occurrence during last year's men's Asia Cup final at the same venue, where the Indian men's team also declined to accept the trophy from Naqvi.
Instead of the official ceremony, the Indian women's team held a private medal presentation. BCCI secretary Devajit Saikia and vice-president Rajeev Shukla were present for the internal awards.

The decision stems from strained cricketing relations between India and Pakistan following heightened cross-border tensions in May 2025, leading Indian teams to avoid handshakes with Pakistani officials.
Head coach Amol Muzumdar stated that the team fully supports the BCCI's position, emphasizing that being champions is what matters most to the squad.
caption:
Champions without a trophy? 🏆 India's women's team refuses to accept the Asia Cup award from Mohsin Naqvi.

India secured their eighth Women's Asia Cup title by defeating Sri Lanka by 72 runs in the final held in Dubai. However, the victory was overshadowed by a diplomatic standoff during the post-match presentation.

The Indian team refused to receive the trophy or their medals from Asian Cricket Council (ACC) president Mohsin Naqvi, who is also the chairman of the Pakistan Cricket Board and Pakistan's interior minister.

The ceremony was delayed by nearly 50 minutes. While Sri Lankan players received their runners-up medals and cheque from Naqvi, the Indian players abruptly ended their part of the ceremony without collecting the award.

This incident mirrors a similar occurrence during last year's men's Asia Cup final at the same venue, where the Indian men's team also declined to accept the trophy from Naqvi.

Instead of the official ceremony, the Indian women's team held a private medal presentation. BCCI secretary Devajit Saikia and vice-president Rajeev Shukla were present for the internal awards.

The decision stems from strained cricketing relations between India and Pakistan following heightened cross-border tensions in May 2025, leading Indian teams to avoid handshakes with Pakistani officials.

Head coach Amol Muzumdar stated that the team fully supports the BCCI's position, emphasizing that being champions is what matters most to the squad.

headline: Monday morning: Dhaka air 6th worst in world
summary: The capital city's air quality plummeted to dangerous levels on Monday morning, ranking among the top ten worst globally.
details: Dhaka's air quality was ranked as the 6th worst in the world on Monday morning.
The city continues to struggle with severe pollution levels that frequently push it into the 'unhealthy' or 'hazardous' categories.
Residents are often advised to limit outdoor activities and wear masks to protect themselves from the high concentration of pollutants in the air.
The recurring nature of this pollution crisis highlights the ongoing environmental challenges facing the urban center.
